# RS2 v2.0 — INTEGRATED INVESTMENT ANALYSIS: AIRBNB, INC. (ABNB)

**Research budget note (declared up front):** Twelve tool calls were allocated and consumed. Searches that did **not** return usable data and remain **[Unconfirmed]**: US GDP/cycle position, credit spreads, short interest & float, insider transactions, options skew, sanctions/regulatory enforcement detail, ABNB segment-level revenue (the pack itself declares this absent), and any long-term (post-2027) company financial framework. Every gap is carried into the scenarios rather than filled with a placeholder.

```
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 0. ANALYSIS OVERVIEW
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

T0 REFERENCE POINT (all valuation is anchored here)
  Price                    $169.63          [Actual - vendor, 2026-09-10 15:14]
  Shares outstanding       590,000,000      [Aggregator - unverified basis]
  Market capitalisation    $100.082B        [Actual - vendor]
  Shares used in DCF       600,000,000      [Assumption - 590M filed outstanding plus
                                             a modest net-dilution allowance; SBC is
                                             ALREADY deducted in full in the cash flow,
                                             so further share-count modelling would
                                             double-count the dilution cost.]

T-1 REFERENCE POINT (last filed fiscal year)
  FY2025                   Revenue $12.241B | Net income $2.511B | OCF $4.646B
                           SBC $1.592B | Operating margin +20.8%   [Actual - pack S.5]

TTM REFERENCE POINT (through 2026-06-30)
  Revenue $13.159B | Net income $2.691B | OCF $4.860B | Capex $0.038B
  FCF $4.822B (36.6% of revenue)                                  [Actual - pack S.3]

Tpf (post-period) REFERENCE POINT
  FY2026 guidance RAISED at the Q2 2026 print (2026-08-06): revenue growth
  "at least mid-teens"; adjusted EBITDA margin "at least 35.5%".
  Q3 2026 guided to $4.69-4.77B (+15% to +17%).           [Actual - company call]
  Stock +9% in extended trading on the print.             [Actual - CNBC]

STEP 0-1. ARCHETYPE: B — QUALITY COMPOUNDER (with an Option-Led overlay
          deliberately EXCLUDED from base intrinsic value)

  Justification (three or more reasons):
  1. Asset-light two-sided marketplace. Capex is $0.038B on $13.159B of TTM
     revenue = 0.29% of revenue. There is no hardware, no fleet, no plant.
     The Product-Platform Hybrid archetype (D) requires a hardware core; ABNB
     has none. D is rejected.
  2. Capital returns are structurally high. Adjusted ROIC is estimated at
     ~47% on a crude operating-capital base (Section 2.5). Net debt is
     negative on the balance sheet. This is the Quality Compounder signature.
  3. Cash conversion is extreme: FCF is 36.6% of revenue TTM; operating margin
     has a seven-year median of 15.3% and a latest reading of 20.8%.
  4. Growth is not a turnaround or a cycle-recovery story; it is a functioning
     compounding franchise with 7 years of continuous revenue growth from
     $4.805B (2019) to $12.241B (2025).

STEP 0-2. VALUATION ENGINE: ENGINE 1 — DCF + Multiples.

STEP 0-3. TRANSITION DETERMINATION.
  A case exists for B -> D as the installed base is monetised (Experiences
  supply +80% YoY, hotel nights growing ~3x the homes business, ~35% of
  first-time hotel bookers converting to homes within a year). Assessed
  against the stated triggers:
    Core revenue >50% of total .................. UNVERIFIABLE (no segment data)
    GM >30% ..................................... UNVERIFIABLE (gross profit
                                                   column is 'not available'
                                                   for every year in S.5)
    FCF+ for 2 consecutive quarters ............. MET
  Verdict: FEWER THAN 50% OF CRITERIA ARE TESTABLE, LET ALONE MET.
  Blended Engine weighting is therefore NOT applied — a blend cannot be
  honestly calibrated on untestable criteria. Engine 1 stands, and the
  Experiences/Services/whole-home-installed-base optionality is treated as
  an OFF-BALANCE-SHEET OPTION, excluded from base IV per Mandatory Rule 6
  ("no mixing core monetisation with future optionality"), and priced only
  qualitatively in Section 3.5 and the Bull scenario.

STEP 0-4. WHY THIS ENGINE.
  * Engine 4 (Expectation-Driven) would be the error: it would allow the
    Ecosystem/Execution bridge to be capitalised at an assumed probability
    with no segment disclosure to anchor attribution. The pack explicitly
    does not hold segment revenue or margin (Section 12). Engine 4 would
    therefore manufacture the premium it is meant to test.
  * Engine 2 (Cycle-Adjusted) would be the second error: travel is
    economically sensitive, but ABNB has no inventory, no fleet and no
    material fixed cost base to normalise. There is no "mid-cycle EPS"
    construct available.
  * Engine 1 is correct because the asset is a cash-flow stream that can be
    forecast directly, and because 71% of the resulting value is terminal
    value — which is precisely the exposure that must be made explicit rather
    than hidden inside a platform premium.

METHODOLOGY DISCLOSURE (declared, not buried):
  Engine 1 is applied on a CASH-FLOW basis, not on a fully intangibles-
  adjusted capital basis. R&D is NOT broken out in the data pack, so the
  Layer 2.5 R&D-capitalisation step is not executable. This is a genuine
  limitation, not a choice, and it is carried into the Audit as a fail.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 1. MACRO CONTEXT
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 1-1. MACRO VARIABLE CHECK   (T0 = 2026-09-10)

  10Y UST yield                 4.87% on 2026-09-10, +0.03pp on the day.
                                Day range 4.827%-4.867%; prev close 4.84%.
                                [Actual - Trading Economics / CNBC quote page]
                                DIRECTION: high and rising, in the upper end of
                                its post-2022 range.
  Real 10Y yield                4.87% - 3.4% = +1.47%      [Estimate - arithmetic
                                on two Actuals]
  Inflation                     July 2026 CPI +0.1% m/m; annual rate 3.4% in
                                July, expected to hold at 3.4% in August
                                (Aug print scheduled 2026-09-11).
                                [Actual - BLS; Estimate - Trading Economics]
  Fed stance                    HOLDING. Reuters (2026-09-09): the Fed "will
                                hold its interest rate steady at its September
                                15-16 meeting and for the rest of this year",
                                with a rising number of analysts seeing AT LEAST
                                ONE HIKE in 2026.  [Actual - Reuters headline]
                                This is a HAWKISH HOLD, not an easing cycle.
                                My prior of "Easing" is REJECTED by the data.
  DXY                           98.91 (2026-09-10), +0.09% d/d, but weaker
                                over the past month.  [Actual - Trading Econ.]
  Global liquidity              [Unconfirmed] - not retrieved.
  Credit spreads                [Unconfirmed] - not retrieved.
  Economic cycle position       [Unconfirmed] - GDP data not retrieved. The
                                combination of 4.87% nominal 10Y + 3.4% CPI +
                                hawkish hold is inconsistent with early-cycle.
                                [Assumption: late expansion / sticky plateau.]

STEP 1-2. REGIME PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTION   [Assumption - calibrated to
                                              retrieved macro Actuals]

  Reflation   (High Rates + Growth)  40%   -> FAVOURED: Cyclical, Value, Financial
  Stagflation (High Rates + Low Growth) 30% -> FAVOURED: Quality, Defensive, Real Assets
  Goldilocks  (Low Rates + Growth)   20%   -> FAVOURED: Growth, Tech, Long Duration
  Recession   (Low Rates + Low Growth) 10% -> FAVOURED: Duration, Bond Proxy, Staples
                                            TOTAL = 100%

  Note the structural point: 70% of the probability mass sits in HIGH-RATE
  regimes. Both of the regimes that favour long-duration equity (Goldilocks,
  Recession) are the low-rate ones, and together they hold only 30%.
  This is a materially adverse distribution for a 32x-owner-FCF asset.

STEP 1-3. ABNB MACRO SENSITIVITY   (-3 to +3)

  Interest rate sensitivity    -2   Long-duration cash flows; 71% of DCF value
                                    is terminal (Section 3). Also consumer
                                    credit sensitivity via RNPL (>20% of GBV).
  Dollar sensitivity           -1   ~50% of GBV is non-US (LatAm +20%, APAC
                                    high-teens, per Q2 2026 call). A stronger
                                    dollar is a translation headwind. Current
                                    DXY trend (weakening) is a mild tailwind.
  Liquidity sensitivity        -2   Discretionary travel demand; multiple
                                    compression channel is the dominant risk.
  Economic cycle sensitivity   -2   Travel is highly discretionary. Mitigant:
                                    ABNB has historically taken share from
                                    hotels in downturns.  [Estimate]
  Commodity sensitivity         0   No direct commodity input; jet fuel affects
                                    the substitute good (flights), not ABNB's
                                    cost base.
  Row average                  -1.4

STEP 1-4. MACRO ALIGNMENT JUDGMENT

  Expected macro impact, regime-weighted:
    0.20 x (+0.3 Goldilocks) + 0.40 x (-0.3 Reflation)
    + 0.30 x (-0.8 Stagflation) + 0.10 x (-2.0 Recession)
    = 0.06 - 0.12 - 0.24 - 0.20 = -0.50

  JUDGMENT: HEADWIND.
  -> Conviction adjusted -0.5 steps (Section 5).
  -> Split-entry discipline strengthened (Section 12).
  -> Per Layer 1 rules, macro does NOT change intrinsic value. It changes
     sizing and entry timing only. It is recorded here and nowhere else.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 1.5. BASE RATE CHECK
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 1.5-1. BASE RATES APPLIED

  Quality-Compounder / Engine 1, 5-year survival .................. 92-95%
  Consumer internet platform sustaining >15% revenue growth for a
    further 5 years .............................................. 20-30%
  Consumer internet platform holding >30% FCF margin for 5 years .. ~50%
  Platform-to-ecosystem monetisation transition succeeding .......... 20-30%
  Company already at $12B+ revenue decelerating to high-single-digit
    growth within 5 years .......................................... ~60-70%

STEP 1.5-2. DEVIATION FROM BASE RATE

  My Base case applies a 9% revenue CAGR from 2026 to 2031, versus a
  trailing 5-year actual CAGR of +29.4% [Actual - pack S.7] and FY2026
  guidance of "at least mid-teens" [Actual - company]. My base case is
  therefore a DECELERATION from both the historical trend and the current
  guidance. That is a deviation in the CONSERVATIVE direction, and it is
  justified by three company-specific facts:
  1. Core markets have already decelerated: US, France, UK, Australia
     bookings growth was in the HIGH SINGLE DIGITS in Q2 2026, while
     expansion markets (LatAm ~+20%) carry the growth.  [Actual - company call]
  2. Take rate is FLAT at 13.2% YoY and was explicitly attributed to FX and
     RNPL payment timing. There is no evidence of pricing leverage over the
     guest or host beyond GDP-like growth.  [Actual - company call]
  3. Nights & Seats Booked grew 10% in Q2 2026 while ADR grew 5%; revenue
     growth of ~15% is the sum. As ADR normalises toward CPI (3.4%) and
     nights growth converges toward global travel-market growth, the
     mechanical ceiling on revenue growth is high-single-digit to
     low-double-digit.  [Actual inputs; Assumption on convergence]

STEP 1.5-3. BASE RATE SHOCK CHECK

  Am I claiming a success probability >1.5x the relevant base rate? NO.
  My Bull case (25% weight) assumes the 20-30% platform-growth base rate
  resolves favourably. My expected value is BELOW the market price, so there
  is no upward base-rate shock flag. There is, however, a DOWNWARD flag worth
  naming: the market price requires an outcome in the top ~20-25% of the base
  distribution, which is exactly the Bull case I have weighted at 25%.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2. BUSINESS QUALITY
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 2-1. BUSINESS UNDERSTANDING

  In three sentences: Airbnb operates the world's largest two-sided short-term
  accommodation marketplace, connecting 8 million listings across 220+ countries
  with guests, and retaining a ~13.2% take rate of Gross Booking Value as revenue.
  It owns no real estate and employs no hosts; its product is matching, trust
  (reviews, payments, insurance), and increasingly the mobile application
  (64% of nights booked on-app, up from 59%).
  It is now extending from homes into hotels (single-digit % of nights, growing
  ~3x the homes rate), Experiences (+80% supply YoY) and Reserve Now, Pay Later
  (>20% of GBV).

  UNDERSTANDABILITY: HIGH. Single revenue mechanism (take rate x GBV), no
  segment opacity that matters to the cash-flow forecast (though it matters to
  optionality pricing, which I have excluded). Analysis reliability is NOT
  downgraded on comprehension grounds.

STEP 2-2. MOAT ASSESSMENT AND MOAT DYNAMICS   (0-3 each)

  TYPE                     SCORE   DIRECTION     EVIDENCE
  Intangible assets/Brand    2     Stable        8M listings, "Guest Favorites";
                                                 brand is strong in supply, weaker
                                                 as a consumer destination brand
                                                 vs Booking.
  Switching costs            1     Stable        Low for guests (multi-homing to
                                                 Booking/VRBO is trivial); moderate
                                                 for hosts with review history.
  Network effects            3     WIDENING      App nights +23% YoY; 11% first-
                                                 time booker growth (4-year high);
                                                 RNPL >20% of GBV; hotel->home
                                                 conversion ~35%.
  Cost advantage             1     Widening      16% YoY decline in customer
                                                 support cost per booking; AI
                                                 resolving ~45% of inquiries.
  Economies of scale         2     Widening      Fixed product cost spread over
                                                 growing GBV; 80% more features
                                                 shipped with flat headcount
                                                 implied.  [Estimate]
  Regulatory barriers        1     NARROWING     Regulation is a NET NEGATIVE, not
                                                 a moat. CEO: "policy is a risk
                                                 that the company will manage
                                                 forever."  [Actual - call]
  Data moat                  2     Widening      Two-sided pricing/recommendation
                                                 data; 50+ language AI assistant.
  ------------------------------------------------
  TOTAL                     12 / 21   => WIDE MOAT (lower bound)
  Adjustment: because the single largest directional risk (regulatory) is
  NARROWING and untestable in magnitude, I record the moat as
  WIDE-BUT-ERODING-AT-THE-EDGE rather than cleanly Wide.

STEP 2-3. LYNCH CLASSIFICATION: FAST GROWER

  Core checkpoints for a Fast Grower:
  * Sustainable growth rate without balance-sheet strain: PASS — internally
    funded, net cash positive, capex 0.29% of revenue.
  * Margin trajectory: PASS THROUGH 2026 (guidance raised to >=35.5% adj.
    EBITDA margin); but the GAAP-to-adjusted gap is ~15pp, of which SBC is
    ~13pp of revenue (S.2.5). This is the central quality caveat.
  * Whether growth is decaying: MIXED — revenue re-accelerated to +17.1% in
    H1 2026 (from +10.3% in FY2025), but nights growth of 10% is the true
    volume signal and is decelerating versus 2024.

STEP 2-4. FINANCIAL STRENGTH SCORECARD

  Metric                              Value                    Tag     Verdict
  Revenue CAGR, 5 fiscal years        +29.4%                   Actual  Excellent
  Revenue growth, H1 2026 YoY         +17.1% ($6.286B vs
                                      $5.368B)  [Arithmetic]   Actual  Excellent
  Operating margin, latest            +20.8%                   Actual  Good
  Operating margin, 7-yr median       +15.3%                   Actual  Good
  ROE (FY2025 NI/equity)              30.6%  [Arithmetic]      Est.    Excellent
  Adjusted ROIC                       ~47% (Section 2.5)       Est.    Excellent
  FCF margin, TTM                     36.6%                    Actual  Excellent
  SBC / revenue, FY2025               13.0%                    Actual  CONCERNING
  Net debt / EBITDA                   Net cash position         Actual  Excellent
  Piotroski F-score                   5 / 7 evaluable checks   Actual  Good
  Accruals ratio (FY2025)             -0.0989                  Actual  Good
                                      (negative = profit is cash-backed)

  OVERALL: EXCELLENT ON CASH, GOOD ON MARGIN, CONCERNING ON COMPENSATION.
  The single item that prevents an unqualified "Excellent" is SBC at 13.0% of
  revenue. It is not a footnote: it is the difference between a 36.6% and a
  ~23.9% owner-FCF margin (Section 2.5).

STEP 2-5. CAPITAL ALLOCATION SCORECARD   (0-3 each, /15)

  1. Buyback efficiency .................... 1 / 3
     $1.1B repurchased in Q2 2026 alone; $3.4B remaining authorisation
     [Actual]. Buying at ~32x SBC-adjusted FCF and roughly AT consensus price
     targets (Section 5.5) is not a value-accretive use of capital. Partial
     credit because the buyback does offset dilution: wtd-avg shares fell from
     680M (2022) to 623M (2025), ~3.2% p.a.  [Actual - pack S.6]
  2. M&A track record ...................... 2 / 3
     Essentially no material M&A; no impairment history in the pack; no
     evidence either way.  [Unconfirmed on any >$1B deal]
  3. Capex efficiency ...................... 3 / 3
     Capex $0.038B on $13.159B TTM revenue. Incremental ROIC far above the
     ~10% WACC.  [Actual]
  4. Rationality of mix .................... 1 / 3
     No dividend, ~100% of FCF to buybacks — while SBC of $1.592B/yr is
     ~39% of the FY2025 OCF of $4.646B. The company is substantially buying
     back the stock it issues to employees. Net shareholder return is real
     but far smaller than the headline buyback number suggests.
  5. Guidance accuracy ..................... 3 / 3
     FY2026 guidance RAISED at the Q2 print (revenue outlook lifted from
     low-to-mid-teens to at-least-mid-teens; margin floor lifted to 35.5%).
     Management exceeded its own outlook "across every key metric."
     [Actual - company call]
  ------------------------------------------------------------------
  SUBTOTAL 10 / 15  => GOOD

  Insider ownership / activity: [Unconfirmed] - not retrieved within budget.
  No +1 or -2 adjustment is applied, and none is invented.
  Effective score: 10 / 15, GOOD.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2.5. INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 2.5-1. R&D CAPITALISATION ......... NOT EXECUTABLE.
  Airbnb does not break out R&D in the data pack, and Section 12 confirms
  segment/line-item detail is absent. Product and engineering spend is
  embedded in SG&A ($1.342B in FY2025). Capitalising an unquantified number
  would be a fabricated adjustment. DECLARED AS A LIMITATION. This means my
  adjusted ROIC below is a cash-based estimate, not a full EVA-style
  calculation.

STEP 2.5-2. SBC — PROPER TREATMENT   *** THE CENTRAL ADJUSTMENT ***

  FY     Revenue   SBC      SBC/Rev
  2019   $4.805B   $0.098B   2.0%
  2020   $3.378B   $3.002B  88.9%   (IPO year — ignore for trend)
  2021   $5.992B   $0.899B  15.0%
  2022   $8.399B   $0.930B  11.1%
  2023   $9.917B   $1.120B  11.3%
  2024  $11.102B   $1.407B  12.7%
  2025  $12.241B   $1.592B  13.0%   [Actual - pack S.5]
  TTM   $13.159B   ~$1.68B  12.8%   [Estimate - extrapolated from the filed
                                     series; SBC grows ~13%/yr]

  ADJUSTED FCF (the number that matters):
    Reported TTM FCF                              $4.822B
    Less SBC (treated as a full cash-equivalent) -$1.680B
    ------------------------------------------------
    ADJUSTED OWNER FCF, TTM                       $3.142B
    => 23.9% of revenue, versus a reported 36.6%.

  The reported FCF figure OVERSTATES distributable owner earnings by 35%.
  Every multiple in this report uses the adjusted figure. The 35 percentage
  point-of-revenue difference between the GAAP operating margin (+20.8%) and
  the adjusted EBITDA margin (35.5%) is dominated by this one item.

STEP 2.5-3. OPERATING LEASE CAPITALISATION
  FY2025 operating leases: $0.272B (down from $0.487B in 2020).  [Actual S.6B]
  Added to debt, this is immaterial: adjusted gross debt = $1.999B current
  portion + $0.272B leases = $2.271B.

STEP 2.5-4. BRAND / DATA ASSET ESTIMATION ......... NOT PERFORMED.
  No defensible Interbrand-style or data-unit-price input is available, and
  any number produced would be a guess dressed as a measurement.

STEP 2.5-5. ADJUSTED ROIC

  FY2025 NOPAT (est.) = Operating income $2.544B x (1 - 21% assumed tax)
                      = $2.010B                        [Assumption: 21% rate.
                      The pack WITHHELD the effective tax rate; I derive it
                      myself and label it my own assumption, exactly as the
                      pack instructs.]
  Operating invested capital (est.) = Total assets $22.208B
                                    - cash $13.486B
                                    - short-term investments $4.454B
                                    = $4.268B            [Arithmetic on Actuals]
  ADJUSTED ROIC = 2.010 / 4.268 = 47.1%               [Estimate]

  Contrast with GAAP ROIC (using book equity + debt as the denominator):
  2.010 / (8.199 + 1.999) = 19.7%.                       [Estimate]

  GAP EXPLANATION (>5pp): the gap is entirely the ~$17.9B of cash and
  short-term investments sitting on the balance sheet earning ~4-5%. It is a
  denominator artefact, not an operating difference. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: a
  material part of that $17.9B is guest funds received but not yet earned,
  which sit in current liabilities ($13.649B at FY2025). The true
  shareholder-attributable cash is therefore MATERIALLY LESS than the headline
  $17.9B. I cannot isolate the unearned-fee balance from this pack. This is
  the reason my net-cash credit in Section 3 is $6B, not $16B.

STEP 2.5-6. OWNER EARNINGS (BUFFETT STYLE)

  TTM: Net income $2.691B + D&A ~$0.10B - maintenance capex $0.038B
       - SBC $1.680B = $1.073B
  Versus the OCF-based adjusted FCF of $3.142B.

  The $2.07B gap between the two is the working-capital / non-cash swing:
  TTM OCF ($4.860B) exceeds TTM net income ($2.691B) by $2.169B
  [Arithmetic, pack S.3], of which SBC is ~$1.68B and the remainder is a
  working-capital benefit driven by unearned-fee float.

  TREATMENT: I use the OCF-based $3.142B as the primary owner-earnings figure
  because the accruals ratio (-0.0989) confirms earnings are cash-conservative.
  BUT I model the working-capital contribution EXPLICITLY and decaying, because
  FY2025's change in working capital was a $1.871B INFLOW [Arithmetic, pack
  S.6] — a one-off-scale float benefit that cannot be assumed to repeat at that
  magnitude. Assuming it repeats is the single easiest way to overstate this
  valuation, and it is not done here.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 3. VALUATION — ENGINE 1 (DCF + MULTIPLES)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 3-1. DISCOUNT RATE DERIVATION

  Risk-free rate            4.87%   [Actual - 10Y UST, 2026-09-10]
  Equity risk premium       4.50%   [Assumption - standard mature-market ERP.
                                     NOT retrieved. Labeled as assumption.]
  Beta                      1.137   [Aggregator - vendor does not state its
                                     window or benchmark. Used as given and
                                     flagged.]
  Cost of equity = 4.87% + 1.137 x 4.50% = 10.0%   [Estimate]

  Cost of debt              5.50%   [Assumption - convertible notes; the $1.999B
                                     current portion matures in 2026, after
                                     which the capital structure is
                                     effectively all-equity.]
  Tax shield                n/a      Debt is de minimis post-2026.
  Capital structure         ~97/3 equity/debt  [Estimate]

  BASE WACC = 10.0%          [Estimate]
  Cross-check: 10.0% WACC against a 4.87% risk-free implies an equity risk
  premium of ~4.5%, which is a historically normal ERP. It is a CONSERVATIVE-
  BUT-DEFENSIBLE rate, not a punitive one. A 10.0% rate is the market-
  consistent rate at today's Treasury yield, not a haircut I have imposed.

  TERMINAL GROWTH = 3.0%     [Assumption]
  Rule check: terminal growth must be <= long-run nominal GDP. US nominal GDP
  growth is ~3.5-4.0% (2% real + 3.4% current CPI, converging toward 2.5%
  over time). 3.0% is therefore at or BELOW the ceiling. Compliant.

STEP 3-2. REVENUE FORECAST — WITH EXPLICIT DRIVER SOURCING

  FY2026: $14.150B (+15.6%).
    SOURCE: COMPANY GUIDANCE. "At least mid-teens" revenue growth for FY2026,
    raised from low-to-mid-teens  [Actual, 2026-08-06 call].
    Cross-check (Arithmetic): H1 2026 actual revenue = $2.678B + $3.608B =
    $6.286B (+17.1% YoY) [Actual, pack S.4]. Q3 2026 guidance midpoint
    $4.73B (+15.5% vs Q3 2025's $4.095B) [Actual, company; note the vendor
    restatement of "about 14%" is inconsistent with the company's own 15-17%
    range and the arithmetic — I use the company range and the arithmetic].
    9M 2026 = $11.016B, implying Q4 2026 of ~$3.134B (+12.8% vs Q4 2025's
    $2.778B) to reach $14.150B. Q4 is seasonally the weakest and slowest-
    growing quarter, so this is internally consistent.
    My $14.150B sits at the LOW-MID of the company's implied range
    ($13.9B-14.4B). The word "at least" means the guidance skew is upward;
    I do not take that skew.

  FY2027-2031: *** NOT GUIDED. NO COMPANY FORECAST EXISTS. ***
    This is the honest and most important statement in the report. Airbnb has
    issued guidance for FY2026 and Q3 2026 only. There is NO FY2027, FY2028
    or long-range company framework in the public record retrieved. Any
    extrapolation I make past 2026 is MY ASSUMPTION, and it is labelled as
    such and ranged in the Tornado analysis rather than asserted as a point.

    What I DO have as structural anchors (all Actual, from the Q2 2026 call):
      - Nights & Seats Booked +10% YoY (volume)
      - ADR +5% YoY (+4% FX-neutral) (price)
      - Take rate FLAT at 13.2% YoY (no pricing leverage)
```
